main_issue: Where to hold the farewell lunch: keep the Korean barbecue the leaving colleague chose, or switch to somewhere D (no beef at the table) and C (back by 2:30) can manage, such as a zi char place.

A-B.evidence: B pushes to keep the BBQ (turns 8, 14); A rejects it (15); B concedes (16) and then agrees to zi char (20).

A-C.evidence: A asks whether the zi char place will be quick enough for C (21, 24), and C is cautiously okay (25). A offers to pre-order (26). Neither shifted.

A-D.evidence: A first says the place is out (7), briefly wavers (9), then agrees it won't work (13). A endorses D's zi char idea (19).

B-C.evidence: B and C never address each other. B accepts zi char (20) and C says the place might be fast enough (25). The agreement is only implicit.

B-D.evidence: B pushes for options at the BBQ despite D's objection (8, 14). B then concedes (16) and endorses D's zi char proposal (20).

C-D.evidence: C suggests a food court (17), D proposes zi char (18). C raises speed concerns (22, 25), and D proposes a fast place near the MRT (23). C accepts it tentatively (25).
